title: Yog Nidra for Better Sleep
excerpt: How deep rest practices help your body remember safety—and invite natural sleep rhythms.
body:
Sleep is not something we force—it is something we allow. Yog Nidra creates the conditions for your nervous system to downshift, releasing the grip of the day.

In practice, you are guided through body awareness, breath, and gentle visualization. There is nothing to achieve. Simply receive.

Try a 20-minute session before bed, dim the lights, and let the practice end without jumping back to screens. Over time, your body learns this as a signal: it is safe to rest.

title: Breathwork for Anxiety: A Gentle Start
excerpt: Simple breathing patterns that calm the mind without overwhelming a sensitive system.
body:
When anxiety is high, long breath holds can feel activating. Start with an even inhale and exhale—perhaps four counts in, four counts out.

Place one hand on your chest and one on your belly. Notice which moves first. There is no wrong answer; only information.

Practice for two minutes, then pause. Healing happens in small, repeatable moments—not in perfection.

title: A Soft Self-Care Ritual for Heavy Days
excerpt: On days when everything feels loud, here is a minimal ritual that still counts as care.
body:
Light a candle. Drink warm water. Sit for five minutes without fixing anything.

If movement helps, choose one restorative pose—legs up the wall, supported child's pose—and stay.

Self-care is not productivity. It is permission.
